value: Who plays the instrument on the left?
Look for the long bow crossing the strings.
A violinist plays the violin. A bow makes its strings vibrate.
Think of the word guitar, then add the ending -ist.
A guitarist plays the guitar, usually by plucking or strumming strings.
Which family does the flute belong to?
The family depends on how the sound begins, not the material.
The flute is a woodwind. Air blown across an opening starts its sound.
The player's lips vibrate against a mouthpiece.
A trumpeter buzzes their lips into a mouthpiece. Trumpet is brass.
Which of these can play a melody?
Its bars can play a melody, with higher and lower notes.
A xylophone has wooden bars of different pitches. It is pitched percussion.
Who usually plays a snare drum?
This musician keeps a beat by striking the drum.
A drummer strikes the snare. The wires underneath give its rattling sound.
Listen for a light stream of air carrying the melody.
Hear the airy, breathy tone. That is the flute.
The sound is a rattling rhythm rather than a pitched tune.
Hear the crisp rattle without a clear melody. That is a snare drum.
Follow the smooth, drawn-out sound of a bow on strings.
Hear the sustained bowed strings. That is the violin.
Listen for short notes made by mallets striking wooden bars.
Hear the short wooden-bar notes. That is the xylophone.
Each note begins with a pluck and gently dies away.
Hear each string being plucked, then fading. That is the guitar.
Listen for a bold buzzing tone from a brass instrument.
Hear the bright, brassy buzz. That is the trumpet.
Find an airy melody above a rattling beat.
The flute carries an airy tune while the snare adds a crisp rhythm.
Listen for smooth bowed strings and short notes from wooden bars.
Bowed violin notes overlap with short wooden-bar xylophone notes.
A plucked string melody sits above an unpitched rattling rhythm.
The guitar makes plucked notes while the snare plays the beat.
Find a breathy melody, sustained strings, and an unpitched beat.
Airy flute, bowed violin, and rattling snare make this three-part band.
Listen for a pluck, a wooden tap, and a snare keeping time.
Plucked guitar, wooden-bar xylophone, and snare rhythm play together.
Listen for brass, a breathy woodwind, and pitched percussion.
Brassy trumpet, breathy flute, and wooden-bar xylophone complete the band.
